According to the energy conservation law,
\[ V = U \]
or, \[ mgh = \frac{1}{2} kx^2 \]
or, \[ x^2 = \frac{2mgh}{k} \]
or, \[ x = \sqrt{\frac{2mgh}{k}} = \sqrt{\frac{2 \times 2 \times 9.8 \times 30}{10^5}} \]
∴ \( x = 0.1084 \, m = 10.84 \, cm \) (Ans.)","image":null,"image_url":null},{"label":"d","letter":"d","text":"Mathematically analyze whether total mechanical energy of the stone just before releasing and 2s after release will be equal or not.","marks":4,"answer":"Potential energy of stone before free fall at 30 m height,
\[ V_1 = mgh \]
\[ = 2 \times 9.8 \times 30 = 588 \, J \]
As the stone freely falls from 30 m height so the initial velocity of the stone, \( u = 0 \, ms^{-1} \)
So, Kinetic energy, \[ T_1 = \frac{1}{2} mu^2 = \frac{1}{2} \times 2 \times 0^2 = 0 \]
Total mechanical energy before free fall,
\[ E_1 = V_1 + T_1 = 588 + 0 = 588 \, J \]
If the velocity of stone after 2 sec of free fall is v then,
\[ v = u + gt = 0 + 9.8 \times 2 = 19.6 \, ms^{-1} \]
Kinetic energy after 2 sec,
\[ T_2 = \frac{1}{2} mv^2 = \frac{1}{2} \times 2 \times (19.6)^2 = 384.16 \, J \]
Displacement of stone after 2 sec,
\[ h_2 = ut + \frac{1}{2} gt^2 = 0 \times 2 + \frac{1}{2} \times 9.8 \times 2^2 = 19.6 \, m \]
Height from the ground after 2 sec,
\[ h' = h - h_2 = 30 - 19.6 = 10.4 \, m \]
Potential energy after 2 sec,
\[ V_2 = mgh' = 2 \times 9.8 \times 10.4 = 203.84 \, J \]
Total mechanical energy after 2sec,
\[ E_2 = T_2 + V_2 = (384.16 + 203.84)J = 588 \, J \]
Here, \[ E_1 = E_2 \]
So, it can be said that total mechanical energy of the stone just before releasing and after 2 sec will be equal.

For this, sometimes the ball can turn into a six.","image":null,"image_url":null},{"label":"c","letter":"c","text":"After how much time did the cars collided with each other?","marks":3,"answer":"Let, the collision is occured between two cars after t times. The displacement of 1st car after t time is x m and the displacement of 2nd car is \((200 - x) \, m\).
Here,
\[ x = v_1 t \]
or, \[ x = 15t \]...... (i)
Again,
\[ 200 - x = v_2 t \]
or, \[ 200 - x = 20t \]...... (ii)
from equation (i) and (ii),
\[ x + 200 - x = 15t + 20t \]
or, \[ 35t = 200 \]
or, \[ t = \frac{200}{35} = 5.714 \, s \] (Ans.)","image":null,"image_url":null},{"label":"d","letter":"d","text":"Explain mathematically, whether there will be any change in total energy of the two cars before the collision and after the collision.","marks":4,"answer":"We know,
\[ v_1 = \frac{m_1 - m_2}{m_1 + m_2} u_1 + \frac{2m_2}{m_1 + m_2} u_2 \]
\[ = \frac{m - m}{m + m} \times (15) + \frac{2m}{m + m} \times (-20) \]
\[ = 0 \times (15) + \frac{2m}{2m} \times (-20) = 0 - 20 \]
\[ ∴ v_1 = -20 \, ms^{-1} \]
\[ v_2 = \frac{m_2 - m_1}{m_1 + m_2} u_2 + \frac{2m_1}{m_1 + m_2} u_1 \]
\[ = \frac{m - m}{m + m} \times (-20) + \frac{2m}{m + m} \times (15) \]
\[ = 0 + 15 \]
\[ ∴ v_2 = 15 \, ms^{-1} \]
Total energy before collision,
\[ E = \frac{1}{2} mu_1^2 + \frac{1}{2} mu_2^2 = \frac{1}{2} m \times (15)^2 + \frac{1}{2} m (-20)^2 \]
\[ = 112.5 \, m + 200 \, m = 312.5 \, m \, J \]
Total energy after collision,
\[ E' = \frac{1}{2} mv_1^2 + \frac{1}{2} mv_2^2 = \frac{1}{2} m (-20)^2 + \frac{1}{2} m (15)^2 \]
\[ = 200m + 112.5 \, m = 312.5 \, m \, J \]
Here, \[ E = E' \]
So, There will be no change in total energy of two cars before the collision and after the collision.

[{"label":"a","letter":"a","text":"What is instantaneous speed?","marks":1,"answer":"The ratio of the distance traveled by an object in a very short time interval and the time interval is called the instantaneous speed of the object at that instant.","image":null,"image_url":null},{"label":"b","letter":"b","text":"To drive a car in carpeted street is more advantageous than to drive in a broken road–Explain.","marks":2,"answer":"It is more convenient to drive on a carpeted street than on a broken road. Broken roads have many high and low grooves, as a result the friction force between the wheels of the car and the road increases as well as the speed of the car decreases. On the other hand, the friction on carpeted street is much less. Because there are no ups and downs on carpeted street. As a result, the car is easy to drive.","image":null,"image_url":null},{"label":"c","letter":"c","text":"Calculate the velocity of object ‘A’ at half-height.","marks":3,"answer":"We know, \( v^2 = u^2 + 2gh' \)
or, \( v^2 = 0^2 + 2 \times 9.8 \times 60 \)
or, \( v = \sqrt{1176} \)
or, \( v = 34.29 \, \text{ms}^{-1} \, (\text{Ans.}) \)
Here, Height, h = 120 m, Initial velocity of object A, u = 0 ms\(^{-1}\), Half height, \( h' = \frac{h}{2} = \frac{120}{2} = 60 \, \text{m} \), Let, the velocity at half height = v, Gravitational acceleration, \( g = 9.8 \, \text{ms}^{-2} \).","image":null,"image_url":null},{"label":"d","letter":"d","text":"Analyze whether energy of ‘A’ and ‘B’ will be equal or not while crossing each other.","marks":4,"answer":"Let, the objects A and B cross each other at height h from the ground in time t.
So for the object B,
\[ h = u_{B} t - \frac{1}{2} gt^2 \]
Here, Initial velocity object A, \( u_A = 0 \, \text{ms}^{-1} \)
or, \( h = 30t - \frac{1}{2} gt^2 \)
Initial velocity object B, \( u_B = 30 \, \text{ms}^{-1} \)
Mass of object A, \( m_A = 0.2 \, \text{kg} \)
Mass of object B, \( m_B = 1.913 \, \text{kg} \)
For the object A,
\[ 120 - h = u_A t + \frac{1}{2} gt^2 \]
or, \[ 120 - (30t - \frac{1}{2} gt^2) = 0 \times t + \frac{1}{2} gt^2 \]
or, \[ 120 - 30t + \frac{1}{2} gt^2 = \frac{1}{2} gt^2 \]
or, \[ 120 = 30t \]
or, \[ t = \frac{120}{30} = 4 \, \text{sec} \]
∴ \( h = 30t - \frac{1}{2} gt^2 \)
\[ = 30 \times 4 - \frac{1}{2} \times 9.8 \times (4)^2 = 120 - 78.4 = 41.6 \, \text{m} \]
At h = 41.6 m if the velocity of object B is v\(_B\) then, \( v^2_B = u_B^2 - 2gh = (30)^2 - 2 \times 9.8 \times 41.6 = 84.64 \). If the velocity of object A is v\(_A\) then, \( v^2_A = u^2_A + 2g(120 - h) = 0^2 + 2 \times 9.8 \times (120 - 41.6) = 1536.64 \).
Potential energy of object A, \( U_A = m_A g \times h = 0.2 \times 9.8 \times 41.6 = 81.536 J \)
Kinetic energy of object A, \( K_A = \frac{1}{2} m_A V_A^2 = \frac{1}{2} \times 0.2 \times 1536.64 = 153.664 J \)
∴ Total energy of object A, \( E_A = U_A + K_A = 81.536 + 153.664 = 235.2 J \)
Potential energy of object B, \( U_B = m_B g h = 1.913 \times 9.8 \times 41.6 = 779.89184 J \)
Kinetic energy of object B, \( K_B = \frac{1}{2} m_B V_B^2 = \frac{1}{2} \times 1.913 \times 84.64 = 80.95816 J \)
∴ Total energy of object B, \( E_B = 779.89184 + 80.95816 = 860.85 J \)
Here, \( E_A \neq E_B \)
So, the energy of objects A and B while crossing each other will not be equal.
","image":null,"image_url":null}]

Efficiency of first electric motor, η = \(\frac{\text{active energy}}{\text{input energy}}\) x 100% = \(\frac{2.352 x 10^5}{6 x 10^5}\) x 100% = 0.392 x 100% = 39.2% (Ans.)","image":null,"image_url":null},{"label":"d","letter":"d","text":"Analyze the transformation of energy by determining the power of second motor.","marks":4,"answer":"Output power of 2nd motor, Pout = \(\frac{\text{W}}{\text{t}} = \frac{\text{mgh}}{\text{t}}\) = \(\frac{1200 x 9.8 x 30}{30}\) = 11760 W.
If input power of 2nd motor is Pin then, Efficiency, η = \(\frac{P_{\text{out}}}{P_{\text{in}}}\) or, Pin = \(\frac{P_{\text{out}}}{\eta} = \frac{11760}{0.784}\) = 15000 W.

Output energy of 2nd motor Wout = Pout x t = 11760 x 30 = 3.528 x 10\(^5\) J.

[{"label":"a","letter":"a","text":"What is watt?","marks":1,"answer":"If a machine or person does 1 J work in 1 s, its/his power is called 1 watt or 1W.","image":null,"image_url":null},{"label":"b","letter":"b","text":"Why does the potential energy of a falling body decrease?","marks":2,"answer":"The potential energy of a falling body decreases because its height from the earth's surface decreases gradually. Potential energy depends on height. So, when height decreases, potential energy also decreases.","image":null,"image_url":null},{"label":"c","letter":"c","text":"With how much velocity will the falling body hit the ground? Determine.","marks":3,"answer":"From 'c', the velocity at the moment of touching the ground, v = 78.4 ms\(^{-1}\).
Time at point P, t = 8s.
Kinetic energy after 8s, T\(_1\) = 6146.56 J (from graph).
the potential energy when the object touches the ground at t = 8s, V\(_1\) = 0 J.
Total mechanical energy at t = 8s, E\(_1\) = T\(_1\) + V\(_1\) = (6146.56 + 0) J = 6146.56 J.
Now, if the object's velocity at t = 4s is v\(_2\) then, v\(_2\) = u + gt = 0 + 9.8 x 4 = 39.2 ms\(^{-1}\).
Kinetic energy after 4s, T\(_2\) = \(\frac{1}{2}\) mv\(_2^2\) = \(\frac{1}{2}\) x 2 x (39.2)^2 = 1536.64 J.
If the object falls from height h then, v\(^2\) = u\(^2\) + 2gh or, v\(^2\) = 0\(^2\) + 2gh or, h = \(\frac{v^2}{2g} = \frac{(78.4)^2}{2x 9.8}\) = 313.6 m.
If the displacement after 4s is h' then, h' = ut + \(\frac{1}{2}\) gt\(^2\) = 0 + \(\frac{1}{2}\) x 9.8 x 4\(^2\) = 78.4 m.
Height from the ground after 4s, x = h - h' = (313.6 - 78.4) m = 235.2 m.
Potential energy after 4s, V\(_2\) = mgx = 2 x 9.8 x 235.2 = 4609.92 J.
Total mechanical energy after 4s is, E\(_2\) = T\(_2\) + V\(_2\) = (1536.64 + 4609.92) J = 6146.56 J.
